nodes.label: 8-byte Fixed Header (!BBBBHH)
nodes.rationale: Fixed header with explicit 16-bit lengths instead of MQTT variable-length encoding; simple to parse with recv_exact.

nodes.label: MQTT v3.1.1
nodes.rationale: Used as a reference, not copied; differences listed to show originality (CPA-1).

nodes.label: Per-room Sequence Number
nodes.rationale: Broker-assigned under the room lock so ordering is visible to clients; unique only within a room, hence PUBACK carries the room.

nodes.label: PRESENCE (JOIN/LEAVE/TIMEOUT, $presence)
nodes.rationale: Built-in presence with snapshot on subscribe, unlike MQTT which only has Last Will.

nodes.label: PUBACK (carries room + status)
nodes.rationale: Means the next hop has taken responsibility, not that the user read it.

nodes.label: QoS 0 / QoS 1 (both hops)
nodes.rationale: QoS 1 on both hops so chat is reliable end-to-end; delivery QoS = min(publish QoS, subscription QoS).

nodes.label: Session Retention (120 s)
nodes.rationale: TCP loses nothing while up; loss happens when the connection breaks, so the broker keeps state for 120 s to replay. Trade-off: broker memory and state lost on broker crash.

nodes.label: TCP_NODELAY (disable Nagle)
nodes.rationale: Small chat messages are not delayed by Nagle's algorithm; matters for latency results.

nodes.label: PSCP v1 Specification
nodes.rationale: Authoritative spec written so another group could build a compatible client or broker from it alone (R1).

nodes.label: Dev Dependencies (matplotlib, pytest)
nodes.rationale: Runtime needs only the Python 3.8+ standard library; matplotlib for experiments/plot.py, pytest optional.

nodes.label: Design Tensions (reliability vs latency, binary vs text, state vs simplicity)
nodes.norm_label: design tensions (reliability vs latency, binary vs text, state vs simplicity)

nodes.label: Session vs Connection Split
nodes.rationale: Broker separates Session (survives disconnect) from Connection (one socket); this split is what makes resume work.

nodes.label: Shared reliability module (Outbox + DedupWindow)
nodes.rationale: reliability.py moved to package level so broker and client share identical QoS 1 retransmit and dedup logic.

nodes.label: TCP-only Transport
nodes.rationale: UDP pings rejected: second socket, session matching, false timeouts on loss, and TCP ping proves the chat connection itself is alive. Client-initiated TCP also traverses NAT without port forwarding.

nodes.label: Security: plaintext, no authentication (TLS as future work)
nodes.norm_label: security: plaintext, no authentication (tls as future work)

nodes.label: Sustainability Analysis (bytes saved, kWh)
nodes.rationale: PSCP saves ~36% bytes vs JSON; persistent connection saves ~34% vs new connection per message; uses 0.06 kWh/GB (Aslan et al. 2018, to verify).

nodes.norm_label: 8-byte fixed header (version, type, flags, topic len, message id, payload length)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-width lengths are simpler to parse and frame than MQTT's variable-length remaining length; version in every message makes each packet self-describing; packed with struct format !BBBBHH big-endian.

nodes.label: Per-topic sequence number ordering (room lock)
nodes.rationale: MQTT does not guarantee ordering across publishers; broker stamps a per-room sequence number under a per-room lock so publishes to the same room are serialised while different rooms proceed in parallel.

nodes.label: PSCP (Publish/Subscribe Chat Protocol)
nodes.rationale: Custom application-layer protocol designed by the group rather than reusing HTTP/SMTP/DNS; implemented directly on Python sockets to satisfy Option D (multi-client chat with presence).

nodes.label: QoS 0 / QoS 1 delivery with DUP retransmission

nodes.rationale: QoS 2 not needed for chat; QoS 1 PUBLISH unacknowledged within T=2 s is retransmitted with DUP=1 up to 3 times; broker acks but does not re-forward duplicates.

nodes.rationale: TCP is a byte stream, so receiver reads 8 header bytes then exactly Topic Len + Payload Length bytes to find message boundaries.

nodes.label: Design tension: State vs Simplicity (broker in-memory state)
nodes.norm_label: design tension: state vs simplicity (broker in-memory state)
nodes.rationale: State is unavoidable for presence and ordering, kept only in broker memory; broker crash loses all state and clients must reconnect/resubscribe. Optional: connection reuse vs server resources.

nodes.label: Transport choice: TCP for all message types
nodes.norm_label: transport choice: tcp for all message types
nodes.rationale: Reliability essential for session setup, chat text and subscriptions; UDP would require custom retransmission, duplicate detection, fragmentation and matching UDP pings to TCP sessions; a TCP ping also proves the chat connection is alive.
